office_does: An Asotin County PUD commissioner sits on the three-member elected board that sets policy, budgets and rates for the public water and sewer utility serving Clarkston and the Clarkston Heights area, for a six-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat: board president Judy Ridge, who beat Joe Louis for this seat in 2020, is not on the ballot. Retired PUD field foreman Louis, with about 40 years on the local water system, faces broadcaster and former Clarkston Chamber president Darcy Nelly, who stresses transparency and accountability. Every PUD voter elects the District 1 commissioner.

candidates.summary: Retired field foreman with about 40 years on the Clarkston-area water system under three owners, including the PUD, running to keep updating mains, wells and tanks.
highlights: Worked on the water system from 1976; PUD field foreman from 1999 [S1]
Holds Water Distribution Manager III and Cross Connection Specialist certifications [S1]
Wants to keep updating water services, mains, wells and water tanks [S1]
Lost this seat's 2020 race to Judy Ridge, 3,682 to 5,472 [S5]

candidates.summary: Co-owner of Nelly Broadcasting, a 34-year resident and former president of the Clarkston Chamber of Commerce, running on leadership, transparency and responsible stewardship.
highlights: Co-owns Nelly Broadcasting; works on advertising budgets and proposals with local businesses [S1]
Past president of the Clarkston Chamber of Commerce, the LCSC Alumni Association and the TriState Health Foundation [S1]
Pledges 'strong leadership, transparency, and responsible stewardship' at the PUD [S1]
